sections.h2: What is the Lynchburg real estate tax rate?
sections.html:
The City Assessor's page says the real estate tax rate for 2025 to 2026 is $0.84 per $100 of total assessed value. At that rate, a house assessed at $200,000 carries about $1,680 in annual tax, which is simple arithmetic and not a bill for any parcel.

The same City Assessor page gives the scale of the office's work, as shown below.

The office is open Monday through Friday, 8:30 am to 5 pm, and maintains a ParcelViewer map tool for property details.

sections.h2: Who is responsible for Lynchburg property tax?
sections.html:
The City Assessor values the property, and the City Treasurer bills and collects. The Assessor's page ties the office to Chapter 18-48 of the Lynchburg City Code, Title 58.1 of the Code of Virginia and Article X of the Virginia Constitution, and it keeps an alphabetical ownership tax roll for each July 1 to June 30 period.

Because every parcel is reassessed every two years, a Lynchburg owner can see a value change without having made any improvement. Property transfers and building permits are processed throughout the year, so a new deck or a sale can move a record between reassessments. The office also prepares special appraisal estimates for budgeting and rental studies from time to time, and those are separate from your tax bill.

Ask the Treasurer for the next installment date and the Assessor for the appeal window before you rely on any date you find elsewhere.

sections.h2: What can you do if you think a Lynchburg assessment is wrong?
sections.html:
Start with the Assessor, who lists an Appeals section on the office page. Virginia also gives a correction route in Va. Code 58.1-3980 for errors made by the assessing official or caused by a factual mistake in a general reassessment.

  • The correction request goes to the official who made the assessment.
  • The deadline is three years from the last day of the tax year, or one year from the assessment date, whichever is later.
  • The statute applies to real estate only when the error is the assessor's or a factual error made during reassessment.
  • A disagreement about value alone follows the city's own review process, which the Assessor can explain.

Keep photos, repair bids and comparable sales ready, since any appeal rests on evidence.

sections.h2: Where is Lynchburg and how did it develop?
sections.html:
Lynchburg is an independent city on the James River in the foothills of the Blue Ridge Mountains, near the geographic center of Virginia. Wikipedia lists 49.53 square miles and an elevation of 630 feet, with 79,009 residents in the 2020 census and an estimate of 81,347 for 2025.

John Lynch, a Quaker ferry operator, founded the settlement in 1757. Virginia's General Assembly recognized it in 1786, incorporated it as a town in 1805 and as a city in 1852. Tobacco, trade and later iron and steel manufacturing powered the early economy, and the James River and Kanawha Canal reached the town in 1840.

The river that built the town also flooded it. The article records floods in 1842, 1847, 1870 and 1877, and the floods of 1870 and 1877 destroyed the city's bridges. A house near the river deserves a closer look at drainage than one on a ridge.

sections.h2: Why is Lynchburg called the City of Seven Hills?
sections.html:
Lynchburg's nickname comes from its hilly terrain, which affects lot shapes, driveways and retaining walls. The seven hills are College Hill, Garland Hill, Daniel's Hill, Federal Hill, Diamond Hill, White Rock Hill and Franklin Hill.

The city has ten recognized historic districts, four of them in the downtown residential area, and 40 individually listed National Register buildings. Wikipedia names these local and state districts:

  • Court House Hill-Downtown, Lower Basin and Kemper Street
  • Daniel's Hill, Diamond Hill, Federal Hill and Garland Hill
  • Fifth Street, Pierce Street, Twelfth Street and Rivermont

Owners in a historic district should ask the city planning office what review applies before they sell or renovate.

sections.h2: What is the economy and climate like in Lynchburg?
sections.html:
Lynchburg is a regional center for education, health care and manufacturing. Liberty University, founded in 1971, is described as the largest employer in the Lynchburg region, and the city is also home to the University of Lynchburg, Randolph College, Virginia University of Lynchburg and Central Virginia Community College. The metro area's industries include nuclear technology, pharmaceuticals and material handling, and Centra operates Lynchburg General and Virginia Baptist hospitals.

The climate is humid subtropical. The monthly average runs from 35.9 degrees F in January to 76.0 degrees F in July, with about 27.4 days a year at 90 degrees or higher and snowfall averaging 11.6 inches a season. Roof and heating condition are fair things to document before a showing.

sections.h2: How do roads and transit affect Lynchburg sellers?
sections.html:
Lynchburg is the largest city in Virginia without an Interstate, so buyers rely on U.S. routes. The article lists U.S. 29, U.S. 501, U.S. 221 and U.S. 460, with parts of U.S. 29 upgraded to Interstate standard, and a freeway called the Lynchburg Expressway.

Amtrak and Greyhound use Kemper Street Station, and Lynchburg Regional Airport has American Eagle service to Charlotte.

sections.h2: What does a cash sale of a Lynchburg house involve?
sections.html:
A cash sale skips the lender, so the steps are short. You request an offer, the buyer reviews the house as is, and a title company handles the deed, the tax payoff and the recording at the circuit court clerk.

Before that, gather the latest tax bill, any notice from the Assessor and the names on the deed. If the owner has died, tell us early, because the personal representative's authority has to be documented before a deed can be signed.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid tax when a Lynchburg house sells?
sections.html:
In Virginia the tax lien on real estate ranks ahead of every other lien, so the closing agent pays any delinquent tax out of the seller's proceeds. Va. Code 58.1-3340 requires the purchaser or foreclosure trustee to apply sale proceeds to assessed taxes and levies, penalties and interest included.

The treasurer then releases the lien, and the seller's current year liability is prorated by contract. Under Va. Code 58.1-802 the seller also pays a grantor's tax of 50 cents per $500 of consideration unless buyer and seller agree otherwise, and the clerk of court collects it at recording.

If you are weighing a quick sale, ask for the exact payoff figure from the Treasurer and confirm any lien with the title company before you sign.

faqs.q: What is the Lynchburg property tax rate?
faqs.a: The City Assessor's page lists $0.84 per $100 of assessed value for 2025 to 2026. City Council sets the rate, so confirm it for the current year.

faqs.q: How often does Lynchburg reassess property?
faqs.a: The Assessor says all parcels are reassessed biennially, meaning every two years. Transfers and building permits are processed throughout the year.

faqs.q: Where is the Lynchburg City Assessor's office?
faqs.a: It is at 900 Church Street, Lynchburg, VA 24504, phone 434-455-3830, open Monday through Friday from 8:30 am to 5 pm.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Lynchburg house with property tax owed?
faqs.a: Yes. The tax lien is paid from the sale proceeds at closing, and the treasurer releases it. Get a payoff figure first so the title company can plan for it.

faqs.q: Where do I find Lynchburg due dates and appeal deadlines?
faqs.a: Contact the City Treasurer for due dates and the City Assessor for appeal deadlines.
